answer.text: Must be separated and accounted independently if they meet specific criteria
Are always combined with the host contract
Are treated as off-balance sheet items

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 215 of the NISM Series I Currency Derivatives workbook (December 2025) states that Ind AS 109 requires the embedded derivative component of a non-derivative (host) contract to be separated and accounted for as a standalone derivative when it is not closely related to the host contract. If the embedded derivative cannot be measured reliably on a separate basis, the entire hybrid contract is designated at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL). The Trap: Embedded derivatives are not always combined with the host contract, are not ignored in accounting, and are not off-balance sheet items. Separation depends on whether the embedded derivative is closely related to the host. Note: Only the separation and FVTPL points expressly supported by page 215 are retained; additional separation criteria sometimes cited elsewhere are not used here.
